title: Tuxedo, Magnolia, Oliver and Perez bands
summary: He lists the original Tuxedo Band, Joe Oliver's Magnolia Band, Kid Oliver's and Manuel Perez's Superior band, and their personnel.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Yes, both of those are dead. Thomas Batten. So I left out of there. I went with playing dance music, you know, with the other bands out in town. And the original Tuxedo Band, there's four of us made up that band. Ernest Trepania, the drummer. William Risley and myself. And Oscar Salisant. Right at my porch, we had four pieces organized, the original Tuxedo Band. So I played with the Tuxedo for a good while. And the band that split up. Salisant had a Tuxedo. And Risley had the Tuxedo Band. Each one, they had two. That's what I heard. The Risley Tuxedo and Salisant had Tuxedo. And I played with Joe Oliver. He had the Magnolia Band. Pops was playing bass. You know what the name of those if I can give you? Oh, yes.
If you can remember, it'll be fine.

That's Pops was playing bass. I was playing violin. Arnold DePass playing clarinet. I mean, drums. Dave DePass was playing clarinet. Is that his brother? That his brother. And Eddie Atkins playing trombone.
King Oliver. Joe Oliver was called King Oliver. He was playing trumpet. Did you play guitar or band?
And Louis Kepert played guitar. I played violin. I played violin.

That time. And I played with the Magnolia Band. I played with the Kid Oliver Band, which is set up with different men in there. And I played with Manuel Perez when he had the superior band. Those old fellas, you might know some of them. That's for myself. And Manuel Perez. And, uh, let's see, trombone. Muddy Johnson was playing trombone. Well, Alfred Pico was playing clarinet. Oh, yes.

You know him? Yes. Maybe Matthews was playing drum. I think that's the band there. And, uh, after I went playing, gigging, you know, from one place to another, I had a band there playing with Chris Kelly. We had a good, uh, rough outfit. Oh, yeah.
